title: The well of Rumah
hookLine: Uthman buys a well and makes its water free for all (Tirmidhi)

cards: A bucket on a rope. That's the whole image of today's story. In a report in Tirmidhi, Uthman recalls the early days in Medina.
When the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, came to the city, Uthman says, there was no sweet water to drink except one well, called Rumah, and it had an owner.

The Prophet asked: who will buy the well of Rumah and put his bucket in it alongside the buckets of the Muslims, for something better than it in Paradise? Uthman bought it, he says, with his own money.

teach.b: Listen to how the Prophet phrased it. Not: who will buy the well and own it. Not: who will buy it and hand out water to the poor.
Who will put his bucket alongside the buckets of the Muslims. The owner's bucket goes down the same shaft as everyone else's: no private rope, no first turn, no gate.
Uthman pays, and from then on he drinks the way the poorest person in Medina drinks. Bukhari mentions this well too, in a chapter on endowments, which is where Muslim jurists place gifts like it.
Some gifts are spent once: a meal, a coin. Others keep giving after you hand them over. A well.
Muslims call this sadaqah jariyah, flowing charity, charity that keeps running like water.
A hadith in Sahih Muslim says that when a person dies, their deeds come to an end except three: a flowing charity, knowledge that people benefit from, and a righteous child who prays for them.
Now the hard part of Tirmidhi's report. Uthman tells this story much later, when he is caliph and rebels have him shut up in his own house.
He reminds them of the well he bought for everyone, and says that now they won't let him drink from it.
The water he set free kept flowing to the very people who turned against him, while, in the report, he was left drinking salty water inside.
Once he had made it free, it was free for everyone.

how: Muslims give sadaqah jariyah, ongoing charity, by funding wells, schools, mosques and other endowments (waqf), often in the name of someone who has died.

charity that keeps giving long after it's given

games.q: you've just bought the only sweet-water well in town with your own money. what do you do with it?
o: charge a small fee to get your money back.
let your bucket go in alongside everyone's, free.
keep it for your family and friends.
games.why: Uthman made it free for all, his bucket with everyone's, as the Prophet had asked.

practice: Think beyond a single coin: what could you set flowing?

A skill taught to someone who'll keep it, a tree in the yard, a small regular gift to something that will still help people long after today, or something you own and share, tools, a ride, your Wi-Fi password with a neighbor.
If you pray, hold it with the intention of a flowing charity.

wordCard.voice: Sadaqah jariyah, flowing charity, the gift that keeps giving, like the well Uthman bought so his bucket went in alongside everyone else's. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: flowing charity, a gift that keeps giving after you.
